newsitem.title: SWEDEN: NORDIC SKIING-FINNS SNATCH FIFTH STRAIGHT RELAY WIN.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-FINNS SNATCH FIFTH STRAIGHT RELAY WIN.

text.p: Finland's men won their fifth consecutive World Cup cross-country relay on Sunday and look favourites for the event at next year's world championships in Norway.

Sami Repo gave the Finns a strong start in the first leg before handing over to veteran Harri Kirvesniemi, who outpaced a field including Norway's Anders Eide in the second stage of the 4 x 10-km classical style race.
"The only danger is that we may get in top shape too early," said 38-year-old Kirvesniemi, adding that the championships in Trondheim starting on February 21 was this season's main target.

Mika Myllyla,in the third leg for Finland, showed no trace of last season's stomach trouble, handing over a comfortable lead to Jari Isometsa, who extended it to 40 seconds over second-placed Italy by the finish.

Norway's Bjoern Daehlie set off in the final leg trailing in eighth place, but Saturday's individual race winner quickly moved up the field, overhauling two Swedes in the final approach to snatch third place for his team.

Elena Valbe, who won Saturday's individual 5-km freestyle race, again crossed the finishing line first when favourites Russia took the women's 4 x 5-km relay 30 seconds ahead of Norway and one minute ahead of third-placed Russia II.
